source: Open Archieven (openarchieven.nl), the open API of Coret Genealogie
licence: Open data — Open Archieven publishes its data openly and asks that the HOLDING ARCHIVE be named as the source, which every row here does in its title; no more than four requests a second, and a recognisable program name, both observed.
note: One claim per archive, carrying the places it holds records for and the archive's own record count for each. THESE ARE INDEX ENTRIES, NOT SCANS: a record is a name, a date and a shelf reference, and whether an image exists is the holding archive's business. The API answers at most 200 distinct places to one question, so any answer that came back full was split in half by year and asked again, recursively, until the slices answered under the ceiling. `records` is the archive's own total and is NOT the sum of the places shown; a place's count is the largest figure seen for it across the slices it appeared in, which is used only to order the list.
